cues.zh: systemd 用得相当有效，那就是 cgroups。

cues.en: C groups, for those who haven't seen them, are a Linux mechanism for grouping processes together so that you can then control them in various ways. They're kind of like just the process grouping functionality of jails.
cues.zh: cgroups，对没见过的人来说，是 Linux 里把进程分组的一种机制，这样你就能用各种方式控制它们。它差不多就是 jails 的进程分组功能。

cues.en: But then you can hang jail like isolation off that. You can hang resource constraints off that. You can do a whole bunch of things.
cues.zh: 但之后你可以在此基础上附加类似 jail 的隔离。也可以附加资源限制。能做一大堆事情。

cues.en: And the other neat trick with c groups that System d uses is that instead of the way that Launch d manages a process, System d manages a c group. And if your process is in that c group, it can't ever escape and neither can its children.
cues.zh: systemd 使用 cgroups 的另一个巧妙之处在于：它不像 launchd 那样去管理某个进程，而是管理一个 cgroup。只要你的进程在这个 cgroup 里，它就永远逃不出去，它的子进程也一样。

cues.en: And so system d can actually kill off all processes involved with the service very
cues.zh: 所以 systemd 实际上能非常

cues.en: effectively without any of them managing to escape through double fork tricks.
cues.zh: 有效地杀掉该服务涉及的所有进程，而它们谁也逃不掉，靠双重 fork 的花招也不行。

cues.en: Another thing that systemd does quite well is user level units.
cues.zh: systemd 另一件做得相当好的事，是用户级 unit。

cues.en: If I want to start a service at boot as a user on FreeBSD,
cues.zh: 在 FreeBSD 上，如果我作为普通用户想在开机时启动一个服务，

cues.en: for argument's sake,
cues.zh: 打个比方说，

cues.en: I can either become root and install an RC script that runs it as me, but that requires me to be root,
cues.zh: 我可以先变成 root，装一个 RC 脚本让它以我的身份运行，但那要求我得是 root，

cues.en: Or I can use a trick in cron for... I think there's an at boot or something like that thing that can start it. But, again, that's not going to restart it. Systemd, I can write a unit file, put it in a directory in my home directory, load it, and I now have a restartable service like my IRC Bouncer.
cues.zh: 或者我可以在 cron 里耍个花招……我记得有个 @reboot 之类的东西能启动它。但同样，它不会帮你重启。而在 systemd 里，我可以写一个 unit 文件，放到家目录下的某个目录里，加载它，然后我就有了一个可重启的服务，比如我的 IRC Bouncer。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: the thing is, system d, in a whole bunch of these ways, represents change,
cues.zh: 问题是，systemd 在很多方面都代表着变化，

cues.en: and a lot of it, which brings us to
cues.zh: 而且变化很大，这就引出了

cues.en: the actual tragedy of the peace.
cues.zh: 和平的真正悲剧。

cues.en: Change can be scary,
cues.zh: 变化可能很可怕，

cues.en: especially when it's not under your control,
cues.zh: 尤其当它不受你控制时，

cues.en: and it's really scary when it threatens things that you find familiar.
cues.zh: 而当它威胁到你熟悉的事物时，就真的很可怕。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: I think as,
cues.zh: 我觉得，作为，

cues.en: you know, the kinds of people we are, we have a really complicated relationship with the familiar. We love with the familiar and with change.
cues.zh: 你知道，作为我们这类人，我们和熟悉的事物之间的关系真的很复杂。我们既爱熟悉的事物，也爱变化。

cues.en: We love changing things when we're doing it.
cues.zh: 我们自己在做的时候，特别喜欢改东西。

cues.en: When someone else tells us don't change that, we go, no. No. No. Wait. It's good. But when they come over to us and say, should change this, you go, no. No. Hold on. Hold on.
cues.zh: 可要是别人说“别改那个”，我们就：不行，不行，不行，等等，这样挺好的。但要是他们主动过来说“这个该改”，你就：不行，不行，等等，等等。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: system d represents a lot of disruptive change.
cues.zh: systemd 代表着大量颠覆性的变化。

cues.en: And part of the problem with that is that getting a whole community to change,
cues.zh: 这里部分问题在于，要让整个社区都做出改变，

cues.en: that's really hard.
cues.zh: 真的很难。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: it results in a kind of knee jerk reaction to it.
cues.zh: 这就会引发一种本能的抵触反应。

cues.en: And the problem with those kind of knee jerks is that they lead to things like abuse,
cues.zh: 这种条件反射式反应的问题在于，它会引发辱骂之类的事，

cues.en: and that's not cool.
cues.zh: 这可一点都不酷。

cues.en: You might not like system d, but that doesn't mean you need to, you know, go and send death threats to Leonard. I've never seen any of that coming from any of the BSD camps, which is great,
cues.zh: 你可能不喜欢 systemd，但这不代表你就得，你知道，去给 Leonard 发死亡威胁。我从没见过 BSD 阵营有这种事，这很好，

cues.en: but what I do see is contempt.
cues.zh: 但我确实看到的是蔑视。

cues.en: Contempt isn't cool. Mocking system d is the wrong attitude to take. It's not the kind of sad thing that Linux people have to deal with and how how sorry we are for them that they have system d. We should be looking at going, why did they choose to do that?
cues.zh: 蔑视可不酷。嘲讽 systemd 是错误的态度。这不是说 Linux 人不得不忍受一件可悲的事，我们多为他们有 systemd 感到惋惜。我们应该去想：他们为什么选择这么做？

cues.en: And what I really find problematic is using System D as a recruiting tool for BSD.
cues.zh: 我真正觉得有问题的是，把 System D 当作给 BSD 招募人员的工具。

cues.en: I don't think that that should be done at all, because when you think about the kind of people that we would bring across, if we were to say, come come to BSD,
cues.zh: 我觉得这根本就不该做，因为想想看，如果我们说“来 BSD 吧”，会吸引来什么样的人，

cues.en: we don't change,
cues.zh: “我们不改变，”

cues.en: or come to BSD,
cues.zh: 或者说“来 BSD 吧，”

cues.en: we don't have system D, oh, but we've just come up with a really good idea for something that works like it,
cues.zh: “我们没有 System D，哦，但我们刚想到一个很棒的点子，做一个功能类似的东西，”

cues.en: I don't think that those are the kind of people that we,
cues.zh: 我不觉得那种人是我们……

cues.en: you know, we don't want to bring that attitude into our our thing. And what, again, what I said we should be doing
cues.zh: 你知道，我们不想把那种态度带进我们自己的东西里。而且，我说过我们该做的

cues.en: instead is asking why did they see this as necessary.
cues.zh: 反而是去问，他们为什么觉得这有必要。

cues.en: And the thing is that if you look at it like that, if you don't see it as all those poor Linux people with their terrible init system and go, hang on, they just did that and I don't understand it. Why did they do that? What did they see in it? That
cues.zh: 你得这么看：别把那些 Linux 人当成带着糟糕 init 系统的可怜虫，说什么“等等，他们就这么干了，我搞不懂。他们为什么这么做？他们从中看到了什么？”这样

cues.en: means that we can then look at that and start to find things that we can get out of it.
cues.zh: 意味着我们能借此审视它，并开始找出能从中获得的东西。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 另

cues.en: other thing to be careful of is
cues.zh: 一件要小心的事是

cues.en: the next generation of people, the people that come after us,
cues.zh: 下一代人，也就是我们之后的人，

cues.en: they don't think the way that we think
cues.zh: 他们的想法和我们不一样，

cues.en: necessarily.
cues.zh: 未必一样。

cues.en: A lot of the people who are now coming into, you know, IT and software engineering, they're so much more used to APIs and not library APIs,
cues.zh: 很多现在进入IT和软件工程领域的人，你知道，他们更习惯用的是API，而不是库API，

cues.en: remote procedure call APIs.
cues.zh: 远程过程调用API。

cues.en: They grok things like containers in ways that may seem quite unfamiliar to us. That doesn't mean that containers are bad,
cues.zh: 他们理解容器这类东西的方式，可能让我们觉得相当陌生。这并不意味着容器不好，

cues.en: and it certainly doesn't mean that containers are the same that should be mocked.
cues.zh: 也绝不意味着容器就是那种该被嘲讽的东西。

cues.en: I heard someone describe Kubernetes as the POSIX of the cloud.
cues.zh: 我听人把Kubernetes形容为云端的POSIX。

cues.en: And while that may sound ridiculous at first, I think it's a scary thought when you think about the fact that we can't run Kubernetes,
cues.zh: 虽然乍听之下可能很荒谬，但我认为想到我们无法运行Kubernetes这一事实，就足以令人恐惧，

cues.en: which
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: brings us to the final section.
cues.zh: 引领我们进入最后一部分。

cues.en: What can we get from systemd?
cues.zh: 我们能从systemd中获得什么？

cues.en: I'm not saying that we should adopt it. I don't think that, you know, I think
cues.zh: 我并不是说我们应该采纳它。我不认为，你知道，我认为

cues.en: trying to directly adopt System D is never going to work for us. I don't think the System D upstream project cares.
cues.zh: 试图直接采用System D对我们来说永远行不通。我不认为System D上游项目会关心。

cues.en: That's fine. But picture, if you will,
cues.zh: 那没关系。但请设想一下，

cues.en: a BSD system with a first class message transport. This could be MARC, but MARC has its own set of issues importing across.
cues.zh: 一个拥有顶级消息传输功能的BSD系统。这可以是MARC，但MARC在跨系统导入方面有其自身的一系列问题。

cues.en: In my mind,
cues.zh: 在我看来，

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: main part of the message transport that we can do better than systemd is
cues.zh: 我们能比 systemd 做得更好的消息传输的主要部分，

cues.en: have it be kernel based,
cues.zh: 就是让它基于内核，

cues.en: because that way we can trust that if there's a user ID in the message saying this came from this user, that we know that it actually did because the kernel put it there.
cues.zh: 因为这样一来，如果消息中的用户 ID 表明它来自某个用户，我们就能确信这确实是真的，因为这是内核放进去的。

cues.en: The kernel could also put things like this was the identity of the signed binary that was executing when the message got sent and things like that.
cues.zh: 内核还可以放入这类信息：消息发出时正在执行的已签名二进制的身份，等等。

cues.en: On top of that, we can build an RPC framework.
cues.zh: 在此基础上，我们可以构建一个 RPC 框架。

cues.en: Again,
cues.zh: 再补充一点，

cues.en: Systemd uses debus for this. We don't have to. We could.
cues.zh: Systemd 用 D-Bus 来实现这件事。我们不一定非得这么做，但也可以。

cues.en: But there's also things like Google's RPC built on top of protobuf,
cues.zh: 但还有像 Google 基于 protobuf 构建的 RPC 这样的东西，

cues.en: which has a whole bunch of advantages as well. And
cues.zh: 它同样有一大堆优势。而且

cues.en: one question that I can see some people thinking about is why?
cues.zh: 我猜有些人会想到的一个问题是：为什么？

cues.en: Because system calls are purely kernel based. If you're managing a system, you need an API that can talk to both user space and kernel.
cues.zh: 因为系统调用完全基于内核。如果你在管理系统，就需要一个既能与用户空间、也能与内核通信的 API。

cues.en: And so having the RPC framework means you can delegate things like network management out to a daemon and communicate with it to say, please change this.
cues.zh: 有了 RPC 框架，你就能把网络管理之类的事交给一个守护进程，并通过和它通信来说“请改一下这个”。

cues.en: It be very good to have a proper note... Notion of a service life cycle, automated service management, actually restarting services that that fall over.
cues.zh: 最好能有明确的服务生命周期概念、自动化服务管理，以及服务挂掉后真正能自动重启。

cues.en: And all of these things would give us a level of automation via API that would be truly amazing. If you think about something like a pfSense or a free NAS,
cues.zh: 所有这些都能通过 API 给我们带来真正惊人的自动化水平。想想 pfSense 或 FreeNAS 这样的东西，

cues.en: that instead of having to grovel around with interpreting the output from ifconfig, whether through LibXO or not, but could instead just send messages out to a service bus to say, I'd like to reconfigure things like this now, I think that would be incredibly powerful and would allow a lot more usage of BSD projects in those kind of appliance situations.
cues.zh: 不用再费劲解析 ifconfig 的输出——不管是否借助 LibXO——而是可以直接往服务总线发消息说“我现在想这样重新配置”，我觉得这会非常强大，也能让 BSD 项目在那类设备场景中得到更多使用。

cues.en: And the same kind of thing would also make them work on desktops
cues.zh: 同样地，这也会让它们能在桌面系统上运行

cues.en: and in a whole bunch of other places.
cues.zh: 以及许多其他场景中运行。

cues.en: I think we need to look a lot harder at making containers work, whether that means we turn jails into c groups or whether we do something else or whether we set up an alarm.
cues.zh: 我觉得我们得更加努力地让容器跑起来，不管是把 jail 改成 cgroup，还是做点别的什么，又或者是设个警报。

cues.en: That'll be the phone, mate.
cues.zh: 那应该是电话，老兄。

cues.en: But, yeah, containers, I think, would be very useful. And all of this would give us a BSD system layer.
cues.zh: 不过，没错，我认为容器会非常有用。而所有这些都会给我们带来一个 BSD 系统层。

cues.en: In the same way that that systemd gives one to Linux, we can have a BSD system layer. This doesn't have to be a cross platform project, but it would be kind of neat if it was.
cues.zh: 就像 systemd 为 Linux 提供了系统层一样，我们也可以有一个 BSD 系统层。这不一定非得是个跨平台项目，但如果真是的话，那还挺不错的。

cues.en: And there are even greater heresies that we could steal from System D.
cues.zh: 我们还可以从 systemd 那里偷来更离经叛道的做法。

cues.en: System D's approach to device naming has unpleasant overtones of what I remember as Solaris disk naming with c zero, t zero, whatever,
cues.zh: systemd 的设备命名方式，让我不太愉快地想起记忆中的 Solaris 磁盘命名：c 零、t 零之类的，

cues.en: but it gets you away from the notion that you have to have all your cards plugged in just so, so the probe order works and EM0 is always EM0,
cues.zh: 但它让你摆脱了那种观念：必须把所有板卡都按特定顺序插好，探测顺序才能成立，em0 才永远是 em0，

cues.en: which would mean that you could then paralyze device probing
cues.zh: 这意味着你之后就可以并行化设备探测，

cues.en: because you don't care what unit number it gets. You then just look at it and go, oh, you're in that slot. I will name you this.
cues.zh: 因为你不在乎它拿到什么单元号。你只需看一眼说：哦，你在那个槽位。我就给你起这个名字。

cues.en: And I think that would be very useful.
cues.zh: 我觉得那会非常有用。

cues.en: There's a bunch of log and audit event and event handling that is coming in through various projects, but Systemd's approach to append only binary logging is not such a silly idea.
cues.zh: 现在有很多日志、审计事件和事件处理，通过各种各样的项目进入系统，但 Systemd 那种只追加的二进制日志做法，其实并不是个傻主意。

cues.en: And the other one that I think would be really interesting to look at, and this is really pie in the sky,
cues.zh: 另一个我觉得很值得一看的方向——这真的还只是空中楼阁——

cues.en: when you look at what a MacOS and IOS application looks like, it's nothing like what we write. There is a main function, but you never write it. All it does is it instantiates an object and then instantiates your object, hands it to the application object, and says, Off you go now.
cues.zh: 你看看 MacOS 和 iOS 应用长什么样，它跟我们写的东西完全不一样。里面确实有个 main 函数，但你从来不用写它。它做的事就是实例化一个对象，再实例化你的对象，把它交给应用对象，然后说：去吧。

cues.en: That application delegate object that you create has a bunch of entry points that can say things like, System's running low on memory
cues.zh: 你创建的那个应用委托对象有一堆入口点，可以传达诸如“系统内存不足”这样的信息

cues.en: or,
cues.zh: 或者，

cues.en: the user just unplugged power, or, you're about to go to sleep now,
cues.zh: 用户刚拔掉电源，或者，你即将进入休眠，

cues.en: which means you've got a lot more richness in
cues.zh: 这意味着你在以下方面拥有丰富得多的手段

cues.en: how you can actually... How the application can actually do things. I have no idea what this would look like on our platform, but it's a fascinating thing to think about.
cues.zh: 你实际上可以如何……应用实际上可以如何做事。我不知道这在我们平台上会是什么样，但这是个很值得思考的有趣问题。

cues.en: And so, at the beginning of this, I put up the Wikipedia definition of tragedy, and it mentioned that it provoked catharsis.
cues.zh: 于是，在开头，我展示了维基百科对悲剧的定义，其中提到它会引发宣泄。

cues.en: This is the Wikipedia definition of catharsis,
cues.zh: 这是维基百科对宣泄的定义，

cues.en: a purification or cleansing,
cues.zh: 一种净化或清洗，

cues.en: purging emotions, particularly pity and fear.
cues.zh: 宣泄情绪，尤其是怜悯和恐惧。

cues.en: And what hope
cues.zh: 而我希望

cues.en: to achieve out of this talk is purging not just the fear, but the pity of System D.
cues.zh: 通过这次演讲达成的是，不仅清除恐惧，也清除对 System D 的怜悯。

cues.en: What I hope is that people will go out of here, and instead of slagging off System D and the Linux people who use it, have a look at it.
cues.zh: 我希望大家走出这里后，不要再去抨击 System D 和使用它的 Linux 用户，而是去了解它。

cues.en: See if you can find something you actually like about it. It doesn't have to be all of it, but find some aspect of it that you think would be useful in the project that you work on
cues.zh: 看看能不能找到你真正喜欢它的地方。不必喜欢全部，但找出你认为在你所参与的项目中有用的某个方面

cues.en: and see if you can make that happen.
cues.zh: 然后看看能不能把它实现。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
